articles.title: ‘Maybe I’m just getting older’: Naomi Osaka’s surprising reaction after US Open exit
articles.summary: Tennis News: Naomi Osaka's US Open campaign came to an end in the fourth round, but the former world No. 1 walked away from Flushing Meadows with a sense of perspe.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka's US Open campaign came to an end in the fourth round, but the former world No. 1 walked away from Flushing Meadows with a sense of perspective rather than disappointment.The two-time US Open champion was beaten by Elena Rybakina in a one-sided contest on Monday, ending a run that had also seen Osaka once again capture attention away from the court with a series of eye-catching fashion statements.Yet when she addressed the media after the defeat, Osaka's focus was less on the loss and more on the bigger picture.Asked whether she was disappointed that her exit meant fans would not get to see some of the other fashion looks she may have planned for later rounds, Osaka admitted there was always something in the works."I think there's always something [laughs]. That's a way that I can have fun and sort of just excite myself also. But I'm honestly not disappointed now. It's a very strange feeling. And last year I wasn't that disappointed either. Amanda just played really insane. Maybe I'm just getting older, but I don't feel sad."‘I'm happy I'm taking losses differently’The four-time Grand Slam champion was then asked whether she was surprised by her reaction to the defeat, given that losses had often affected her more deeply earlier in her career.Osaka said she has learned to process setbacks differently and now looks for lessons rather than dwelling on disappointment."I think I'm happy I'm taking losses differently. I'm trying to learn from them a lot more. Today if I was to say I'm sad, I was sad that I couldn't push off on my foot. I'm sad I couldn't do what I set out to do."The 28-year-old revealed she had been troubled by pain in her leg during the match against Rybakina, which affected her movement on court.Still, she stressed that tennis results no longer define her outlook on life."But for me if I think about my life, my daughter is healthy. Everyone in my family is great. I had an opportunity to play this Slam. I got as far as I could. It's only up from here I guess."Osaka's fashion showcase lights up New YorkAlthough her tournament ended in the fourth round, Osaka remained one of the standout personalities of the event thanks to a string of fashion-forward appearances inspired by basketball culture.With sponsor Nike celebrating the New York Knicks' championship triumph, Osaka unveiled a different look throughout the tournament, working alongside celebrity stylist Law Roach.For her final appearance, she arrived on court wearing a fur-trimmed multicoloured cloak designed by Brooklyn-based label KidSuper."I felt really swaggy when I put it on," Osaka said after the match. "I feel feel like it embodied New York a lot."The outfit also featured a headband inspired by the NBA logo, replacing the traditional basketball player silhouette with a tennis player holding a racket.Earlier in the tournament, Osaka paid tribute to NBA legend Allen Iverson with a dramatic first-round ensemble designed by Who Decides War, featuring a long white tulle skirt, a hooded robe and cornrows beneath a headband reminiscent of Iverson's iconic style.Her second-round look came from Thom Browne and included a flowing white jacket embroidered with crossed tennis rackets, while the mesh fabric of her skirt was designed to resemble a basketball net.For the third round, she wore an oversized Monse outfit that blended a suit jacket and hoodie with flowing fleece trousers, combining businesswear and sportswear aesthetics.‘If I win another Grand Slam, it's not going to change my life’Osaka's comments after the loss reflected a broader shift in how she now views her career and achievements.While still motivated to compete at the highest level, the former world No. 1 suggested that winning another major title would not fundamentally alter her life or sense of fulfilment.Reflecting on everything she has already achieved in the sport, Osaka indicated she no longer measures happiness solely through victories and trophies."Maybe I'm just getting older, but I don't feel sad," Osaka said. "I think, also, if I reflect on my career and the things that I've been able to do, there's nothing that I regret or there's nothing that I'm sad about ... If I win another Grand Slam, it's not going to change my life."For Osaka, the US Open may have ended earlier than she hoped, but her reaction to defeat suggested a player increasingly at peace with both her career and her life beyond tennis.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Zverev de siempre ya está en cuartos de final
articles.standfirst: El alemán vuelve a convencer ante Darderi y es el primero en llegar a las 50 victorias esta temporada
articles.summary: El alemán vuelve a convencer ante Darderi y es el primero en llegar a las 50 victorias esta temporada
articles.body: Alexander Zverev continúa con su temporada estelar en los Grand Slam. Por cuarta vez este año, ha certificado su pase a los cuartos de final de un grande, el único jugador en hacerlo. En esta ocasión, ha derrotado al italiano Luciano Darderi por 6-2, 6-2 y 7-6 (3) en otro gran desempeño. Sascha, que en sus dos primeros partidos en Flushing Meadows llegó a sumar 10 horas en pista, ha cambiado el guion de su torneo. En el duelo de tercera ronda con Tabilo, y hoy ante Darderi, ha conseguido dos valiosas victorias en tres mangas. Cabe recordar que los cuatro partidos diputados hasta el momento del alemán, han sido en el segundo turno nocturno de la Arthur Ashe. Condiciones que parecen sentarle bien al tenista de Hamburgo. Zverev tenía muy claro como salir hoy. Agresivo y enchufado desde el primer punto, más si cabe sabiendo de la pegada que tiene el italiano. Todo estuvo marcado por el servicio del alemán, que elevó su porcentaje de primeros hasta un 72%, adjudicándose 51 de 59 (86%) puntos con una de sus mayores armas. Sascha empezó marcando su terreno rompiendo el saque de su rival en el juego inicial del partido. Las dos primeras mangas siguieron la misma tónica, el alemán, incontestable tanto al servicio como al resto, y Darderi sin saber por donde tirar. Hasta 17 bolas de 'break' llegó a fabricarse el primer cabeza de serie del torneo. El tercer set necesitó del tie-break para decidir el último cuartofinalista del cuadro masculino. El italiano había subido de gran manera en el encuentro de la mano de su mejora al primer servicio. Pero la regularidad del alemán tuvo premio (su récord en tie-breaks en 2026 es de 28-13) y lo cerró por 7-3. Zverev, ya con un nivel más parecido al que le hizo campeón en la tierra de París y finalista en Wimbledon, está entre los ocho mejores del US Open. Con sus 19 cuartos de final, Sascha es el segundo tenista en activo que más veces ha pisado esta ronda. Ya ha superado a Stan Wawrinka (18), y solo tiene por encima a Novak Djokovic (66). Su próximo objetivo será el holandés Botic Van de Zandschulp, que viene de derrotar al lucky-loser Arthur Gea en 5:13 h de partido, el cuarto más largo en la historia del torneo.

articles.title: US Open 2026: Home favourite Coco Gauff wins all-American showdown with Iva Jovic to reach quarter-finals
articles.summary: An impressive victory for Coco Gauff sets up a last-eight meeting with French Open champion Mirra Andreeva; Gauff is aiming to win the US Open for a second time in her career; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
The 22-year-old, who is bidding for a second Flushing Meadows title, overpowered Jovic 6-1, 6-4 on a balmy Labour Day bank holiday night in New York.

A jittery start from the 2023 winner gifted 18-year-old Jovic a break in the first game with a double fault.

But Jovic's nerves were also on show as Gauff raced away with the next six games to take the first set.

Jovic finally held serve at the start of the second but three spectacular Gauff hustles, turning desperate defence into all-out attack, secured a break for 3-2.

The youngster managed to hit straight back, but was then broken to love as Gauff took control before serving out to win in an hour and 33 minutes.

Gauff, who is yet to drop a set so far, made sure to reassure Jovic that her time will come: "Iva's an incredible player, an incredible talent, she plays beyond her years. I'm used to being the younger American!

"I thought today was a good match for me. The first set was really high-level and she raised her level in the second.

"I had some opportunities to maybe get up some early breaks. We're all just happy with how I was able to close the last game out.

"I think I just remember when I was that age, every loss was so low, and every win was so high. I think there's lessons to be learned in the losses.

"She seems a little bit more mature than maybe I was at 18, but I feel like sometimes the losses for me felt so low.

"So I think it's just important getting her to know that she's playing good-level tennis, and I think today it just went my way.

"I am someone who played well young too, so it doesn't always matter. Sometimes it does matter, and you just learn those lessons and I know that she will be in many more fourth rounds and quarters, and she'll capitalise on those moments the next time."

Andreeva up next as quarter-final line-up complete

The impressive victory set up a last-eight meeting with French Open champion Mirra Andreeva, whom Gauff has beaten in all five of their career meetings.

With Gauff's win, the woman's quarter final line-up is set as Aryna Sabalenka plays Linda Noskova and Jessica Pegula takes on Emma Navarro.

Gauff then faces Andreeva, with Qinwen Zheng against Elena Rybakina for a place in the final four at Flushing Meadows.

"It is another tough match," Gauff added. "Mirra is someone that I always have tough matches with and they have leaned my way but every match could have almost gone either way.

"She is obviously in a different mindset now at the top of the game coming off of a Grand Slam win. I expect her to approach the match completely differently than she did in the past."

articles.title: US Open 2026: Alexander Zverev reaches quarter-finals in rare pre-midnight finish in New York
articles.summary: World No 87 Arthur Gea missed out on becoming the first lucky loser to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final as he lost to Botic van de Zandschulp, who awaits as Alexander Zverev's last eight opponent; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
The top-seeded German cruised through the opening two sets before fending off a Darderi fightback in the third to win 6-2 6-2 7-6(3).

It would mark the first time Zverev has finished a match before midnight in New York this tournament having played four successive night-session matches, including two five-setters.

The 2020 finalist, who has previously finished games at times of 1:55am, 2:15am and 1:09am, was able to see the funny side of a rare early night at 11.48pm.

"I don't know what to do with ​myself, because it's before midnight," said Zverev. "I might go to a practice court, or a bar... that was a joke, so ‌relax. I'm feeling happy, compared to the first two matches the level has been going up."

Zverev is the only man to reach the quarter-finals of all four Grand Slams this year and will now face Botic van de Zandschulp in the final four following the Dutchman's win over lucky loser Arthur Gea.

"I ⁠thought that my level was consistent, but he started incredibly well in third set," Zverev added of his performance.

"I barely saw anyone hit so hard so consistently. He ⁠made it very difficult for me. I'm ​happy to be in the quarter-finals and playing this way."

Next opponent Van de Zandschulp had denied France's world No 87 Gea the chance to become the first lucky loser to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final in a 3-6 6-7 (0-7) 7-6 (9-7) 7-6 (7-3) 6-4 win lasting five hours and 13 minutes.

"I think he's an impressive player," said Zverev of Van de Zandschulp. "I think this might be his favourite tournament in the world, because I think he made a few quarter-finals here before. Obviously he knows how to play well on these courts, and I look forward to having a tough battle."

Belgium's Alexander Blockx meanwhile fought through injury to beat Argentina's Francisco Cerundolo and reach his first Grand Slam quarter-final.

The 28th seed clinched a 6-3 4-6 7-5 7-5 victory before admitting he considered retiring hurt due to a rib issue.

"It was really tough from the beginning of the match. I was struggling a lot, especially while serving. It kept getting worse throughout the match," said the 21-year-old.

"I was really close to retiring, to be honest. I was just hanging in there, but if I would have lost the third set, I think the chances were really high of me retiring.

He will now play Karen Khachanov after the Russian's 7-5, 4-6, 6-7 (6), 6-1, 6-4 win over the USA's Learner Tien.

articles.title: US Open 2026: Carlos Alcaraz can end American dreams by beating Ben Shelton, plus Frances Tiafoe or Alex Michelsen, in New York
articles.summary: Three Americans have the chance to become the first home US Open men's champion since 2003. But Carlos Alcaraz stands in the way.
articles.body:
It could be Carlos Alcaraz versus the United States over the next few days.

The Spanish superstar's popularity at the US Open might be severely tested if he single-handedly prevents an American having the chance to become the first home men's singles champion in 23 years.

Three American players - Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen - remain in the draw. All three are in the same half as Alcaraz.

On Tuesday, the defending champion takes on eighth seed Shelton in the quarter-finals.

If the seven-time major winner comes through that blockbuster clash, he will face either Tiafoe or Michelsen in the semi-finals.

And if Alcaraz wins again to reach the Flushing Meadows final, the host nation's long wait for somebody to finally follow in Andy Roddick's 2003 footsteps continues.

Alcaraz says he expects to be facing 24,000 New Yorkers on Arthur Ashe Stadium as well as Shelton, who is looking to reach his second US Open semi-final.

"I think he [will] use the crowd, the people behind him, especially when he's playing here at home," said Alcaraz.

If Ashe can help 23-year-old Shelton earn his first career win over Alcaraz, there is guaranteed to be an American player in the final.

Home stars reaching the men's semi-finals has not been uncommon this century, but only Taylor Fritz has reached the final - two years ago when he lost to Jannik Sinner - since Roddick was beaten by Roger Federer in the 2006 final.

Tiafoe, who is seeded 11th, lost to Fritz in another all-American semi-final and was also eliminated by Alcaraz at the same stage in 2022.

Now the 28-year-old is aiming for a third opportunity to reach his first Grand Slam final.

Tiafoe reached the Cincinnati final last month and, thriving off the energy of the New York crowd, has maintained his momentum.

On what it is like to receive such support, he said: "It's an out-of-body experience, no question. No real explaining that type of feeling.

"It's like you're not even touching the ground at one point. Energy is so high, and it seems like the level of play matches that."

While Tiafoe is one of the sport's great entertainers, 22-year-old Michelsen is more understated.

The world number 46 admits he has been happy to fly "under the radar" at Flushing Meadows while the likes of Tiafoe, Shelton, Fritz and Tommy Paul soak up the attention.

But earning a place in a Grand Slam quarter-final for the first time, and not dropping a set on his way, means Michelsen will find himself under the spotlight on Ashe.

"First, second, third rounds, all matches I'm feeling nerves. It's a human experience," he said.

"But it's just about going out there and managing them to the best of my ability. I feel like I've done that very well."

Six men and women from the United States have reached the last eight at Flushing Meadows this year - the highest tally since 2002 - with three players in each draw.

Along with Tiafoe or Michelsen in the men's, the home fans know they are guaranteed to see at least one American reach the women's semi-finals.

Third seed Jessica Pegula, who is yet to land a major title despite her consistency on the WTA Tour, meets Emma Navarro in another all-American clash on Tuesday.

Coco Gauff - who sits on the other side of the draw - can join Pegula or Navarro by beating Russian fifth seed Mirra Andreeva on Wednesday.

But, unlike the men, there is not a long American drought on the women's side.

Gauff, 22, is looking to win the women's title for the second time, having lifted the trophy in 2023 as a teenager to fulfil the promise she had already long shown.

Pegula, 31, was a beaten finalist in 2024 when she lost to Aryna Sabalenka, who also beat Navarro in the semi-finals that year.

Navarro, 25, has not reached the same stage of a major since, but is rediscovering her best form after stepping back from the tour earlier this season because of health issues.

After beating Russian 21st seed Anna Kalinskaya on Ashe in the last 16, Navarro joked she should have tried getting the home fans on her side before facing Pegula.

"I should have talked to the crowd a little, asking them to come back and cheer me on for that match. I'm definitely going to need them," she said.

articles.title: Wimbledon no acreditará a 'influencers' tras los incidentes en el US Open
articles.standfirst: La 'mala praxis' de los creadores de contenido ha provocado críticas por parte de los tenistas y problemas durante algunos partidos
articles.summary: La 'mala praxis' de los creadores de contenido ha provocado críticas por parte de los tenistas y problemas durante algunos partidos
articles.body: El torneo de Wimbledon no acreditará a 'influencers' y se desmarcará de esta manera de las polémicas surgidas en el actual Abierto de Estados Unidos, donde cerca de un centenar de 'creadores de contenido' fueron acreditados por la organización y provocaron problemas durante la disputa de los partidos. El torneo neoyorquino dio el doble de acreditaciones a 'influencers' de cara a esta edición con el objetivo de atraer a una audiencia mayor, pero las prácticas de los mismos han provocado críticas por parte de los tenistas y problemas durante los partidos. Según medios británicos, la organización de Wimbledon no tiene entre sus planes acreditar a 'influencers' o creadores de contenido, como ha sido la norma habitual hasta ahora. Además, las normas del propio All England Club, el recinto donde se disputa el torneo, impiden que se acceda a los partidos con objetos como aros de luz. El personal acreditado de Wimbledon tiene, además, prohibido grabar vídeo en la mayoría de zonas del club. Durante la disputa del US Open, en uno de los partidos de la cuatro veces ganadora de Grand Slam Naomi Osaka, un grupo de 'influencers' utilizó uno de estos aros de luz, distrayendo a las jugadoras, además de que el juez de silla tuvo que llamar la atención al público en varias ocasiones. La japonesa criticó esta actitud, mientras que Coco Gauff animó a que se sigan las reglas de etiqueta del deporte. También ha habido otro tipo de interrupciones durante algunos encuentros de esta edición del US Open. Aryna Sabalenka, número uno del mundo, paró un partido porque supuestamente alguien estaba fumando marihuana en la grada.

At the time, she was already an established name on tour and, to Andreeva, a player she had watched from afar.“Nastya was always like a prodigy. The Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd.Alcaraz expects the packed New York crowd to make life difficult. He knows Shelton will feed off the support from the stands. articles.title: Rafael Nadal’s inspiring family story: How Toni and Miguel Angel Nadal shaped his legendary tennis journey, discipline, humility and success in 22 Grand Slam titles
articles.summary: International Sports News: Explore how Rafa Nadal's uncles Toni and Miguel Angel shaped his journey to becoming a tennis legend, instilling discipline, humility, and the values that led to his success.
articles.body: Rafael Nadal has enjoyed an amazing tennis career, thanks to amazing talent, physical stamina and a competitive spirit like no other. The personality of the 22-time Grand Slam champion was shaped from a young age by a close family in Mallorca, in particular the influence of his uncles Toni Nadal and Miguel Angel Nadal.The Nadal family had influence beyond tennis. Toni was demanding in coaching, instilling lessons in discipline, while Miguel Angel was an example of elite football, professionalism and sporting success. With his parents, Sebastián Nadal and Ana María Parera, the family helped keep the future champion grounded as his fame spread across the globe.How Rafael Nadal’s family shaped his legendary tennis careerNadal’s rise began in Manacor, Mallorca, where tennis was a key part of his childhood. His uncle Toni soon recognised his nephew’s unusual instinct on the court and became the coach who would influence much of his development. Toni worked with Nadal from childhood until 2017 and was in his corner for 16 of his 22 Grand Slam titles.Toni’s methods were tough. Training included repeated practice, physical exertion and an emphasis on concentration, responsibility and improvement. In those days, Nadal’s job was to retrieve tennis balls and tend to his equipment, with junior-level victories regarded as stepping stones rather than reasons to party.The family also opted for stability rather than a quick exit from Mallorca. When Nadal was 14, the family turned down a tennis scholarship that would have required them to move to Barcelona, allowing him to continue to develop in his familiar home environment and coaching framework.How Miguel Angel Nadal influenced Rafael Nadal’s sporting journeyToni Nadal had a direct hand in shaping Rafael’s tennis, but Miguel Angel Nadal was another powerful sporting influence. Miguel Angel, a former defender for FC Barcelona and Spain, was already an established elite athlete before Rafael became a global tennis star. His presence provided the young Nadal with an example of what professional sport required away from the spotlight.Miguel Angel’s career also mirrored the larger athletic milieu that surrounded the Nadal family. It is said Rafael was interested in football as a boy and that his uncle’s footballing success gave him the chance to see top-level competition first-hand. Nadal’s football connection was also a feature of his early sporting identity, before tennis became his clear professional path.Miguel Angel’s role was therefore more than that of a direct coach. He was the family’s established sporting benchmark, demonstrating to Rafael the pressures, discipline and responsibilities of elite sport. Rafael grew up in an atmosphere of professional commitment, as both Toni and Miguel Angel had a background in competitive sport.How Nadal family values shaped Rafael Nadal’s legacyPerhaps the greatest contribution of the Nadal family was to stress the importance of staying grounded. But his family in Mallorca continued to provide the usual surroundings even as Rafael began winning major titles and international recognition. His parents, Sebastián and Ana María, were important people in his life, and his sister Maribel and other family members were part of his support system.Family influenceImpact on Rafael NadalToni NadalDiscipline, endurance, competitiveness and mental strengthMiguel Angel NadalElite sporting example and football influenceSebastián NadalStability and family supportAna María PareraStrong family foundation and personal groundingMaribel NadalClose sibling support and connection to home22 Grand Slam titles are the headline achievement, but the deeper story is the family structure behind the achievement. articles.summary: Our experts predict how the US Open quarterfinal round will unfold, including which American stars will move on to the semifinals.
articles.body:
The 2026 US Open reaches the quarterfinals having delivered everything tennis fans could ask for: dramatic upsets, breakout performances and championship-caliber battles under the lights in New York.

Now, with the tournament entering its final stages, attention turns to the biggest question of all: Who will leave Flushing Meadows with a Grand Slam title?

From tournament favorites and proven champions to dangerous dark horses capable of bigger surprises, our experts give their takes on the men's and women's draws with predictions of the quarterfinal round:

Unforgettable US Open 2026 tennis photos from New York

US Open predictions in women's quarterfinals

There is no reason to get away from previous predictions: Americans Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula will be in the semifinals.

Pegula will dispatch fellow American Emma Navarro in the quarterfinals to set up a date with current Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the semfinals. Noskova will knock out two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka and be partly responsible for Sabalenka losing her No. 1 ranking.

Coco Gauff , meanwhile, will prevail against Mirra Andreeva in a battle of the past two French Open champions, setting up a semifinal match against newly top-ranked Elena Rybakina , the reigning Australian Open champion.

Aryna Sabalenka hasn't dropped a set yet in this tournament, but that streak – and her chance at a U.S. Open three-peat – will end when she loses to this year's Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova . Noskova, as she often does, will come out strong in the first set and lose the second set before bouncing back to defeat Sabalenka and clinch a spot in the U.S. Open semifinals for the first time in her career.

In more bad news for Sabalenka, Elena Rybakina will take over the No. 1 ranking from Sabalenka when she reaches the semifinals by dispatching Qinwen Zhang .

Meanwhile, the two highest ranked American women will both reach the semis as world No. 3 Jessica Pegula takes care of Emma Navarro and world No. 4 Coco Gauff remains undefeated against Mirra Andreeva in their sixth meeting.

US Open predictions in men's quarterfinals

Since the men's draw is more unpredictable, with only three of the 10 seeds making the fourth round, two-time US Open winner Carlos Alcaraz (2022, 2025) is the pick here over Ben Shelton . U.S. fans will still have an American contender, though, as Frances Tiafoe reaches his third US Open semifinal (2022, 2024) after ending Alex Michelsen's longshot bid.

On the other side of the draw, No. 1 Alexander Zverev will continue to cruise, dispatching an exhausted Botic van de Zandschulp , who needed five sets and three tiebreakers Monday to even reach the quarterfinals. Unseeded Karen Khachanov will notch another upset, taking down No. 28 Alexander Blockx , to set up a semifinal clash with Zverev.

Although Ben Shelton has looked like the strongest American contender on the men's side, he won't get past the unflappable defending U.S. Open champion Carlos Alcaraz , who has never dropped a set to Shelton in two previous hard-court meetings. But Alcarez will face another American in the semifinals after Frances Tiafoe ends Alex Michelsen's Cinderella run .

No. 1 seed and late-night session king Alexander Zverev will outlast giant slayer Botic van de Zandschulp . Belgian Alexander Blockx will attempt to battle through his rib injury but ultimately succumb to Karen Khachanov , who will reach his third major semifinal (2022 U.S. Open, 2023 Australian Open).

articles.title: No. 1 in reach as Rybakina battles for US Open semi-final spot
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina is one win away from the world number one ranking, but the Kazakh star says her main goal in her US Open quarter-final clash with Zheng Qinwen...
articles.body:
Elena Rybakina is one win away from the world number one ranking, but the Kazakh star says her main goal in her US Open quarter-final clash with Zheng Qinwen on Wednesday is to advance toward a third Grand Slam title.

"Number one ranking is, of course, one of the goals," Rybakina says. "But I think the main focus for me is to win the titles, and then the ranking will follow up."

Rybakina arrived at Flushing Meadows as one of four women with a chance to supplant Aryna Sabalenka atop the rankings, and the only one with her fate in her own hands. Reaching the semis will send her to the summit for the first time, and she could even get there if she loses -- if Sabalenka, world number three Jessica Pegula and fourth-ranked Coco Gauff all fail to lift the trophy.

Rybakina, who has shown no sign of the foot injury that hindered her US Open preparations, will be out to halt the remarkable run of Zheng -- the Paris Olympics gold medallist who had to come through qualifying thanks to a rankings plunge in the wake of elbow surgery last year.

Gauff, in the quarters for the first time since she won the US Open title in 2023, will take on fifth-seeded French Open champion Mirra Andreeva for a place in the semis while men's top seed Alexander Zverev faces Dutch veteran Botic van de Zandschulp.

Alexander Blockx tries to further his dream US Open debut taking on Russian Karen Khachanov.

AFP Sport looks at Wednesday's action at the US Open

Elena Rybakina (KAZ x2) v Zheng Qinwen (CHN)

Rybakina's four victories over Zheng include two this year, but the former world number one from China is finally on a roll. Counting qualifying Zheng has racked up seven wins in Flushing Meadows, including a dramatic come-from-behind victory over Madison Keys in which she saved a match point as she rallied from 5-0 down in the third set to win with closing run of seven straight games.

She followed with another seven-game surge to salvage the first set in a straight-sets victory over six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek.

"She definitely found her form," Rybakina said. "I feel like she's playing now with a lot of confidence after so many wins in a row, so she's very dangerous."

Coco Gauff (USA x4) v Mirra Andreeva (RUS x5)

Gauff has won all five meetings with the fifth-seeded French Open champion, including a victory on the way to the 2023 US Open title and, most recently, a win in the quarter-finals in Rome.

That was before Andreeva broke through for her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros, and Gauff believes that triumph means she'll be facing a new Andreeva.

"She's obviously in a different mindset now at the top of the game coming off of a Grand Slam win," Gauff said. "I expect her to approach the match completely differently.

"I think it's going to be a really athletic, tough match. Hopefully I can take my opportunities when I get them."

Alexander Zverev (GER x1) v Botic van de Zandschulp (NED)

World number two Zverev knows the 70th-ranked van de Zandschulp is a tricky proposition on the US Open hard courts, where the Dutch player stunned then world number three Carlos Alcaraz in the second round two years ago.

"I think he's an impressive player," Zverev said. "I think this might be his favorite tournament in the world ... Obviously he knows how to play well on these courts"

Zverev himself was slow to fire in Flushing Meadows, laboring through two five-setters to start the tournament before straightforward wins over seeded players Alejandro Tabilo and Luciano Darderi.

"I think after 10 hours on court, I just maybe found my rhythm a little bit better, which is helpful because the first two matches were really not great level," said Zverev, who claimed a long awaited maiden Grand Slam at Roland Garros.

Karen Khachanov (RUS) v Alexander Blockx (BEL x28)

It's a race for fitness for 21-year-old Blockx, who nearly retired from his fourth-round win over Francisco Cerundolo because of a painful rib injury. With the help of mid-match medication he soldiered on, saving 14 of 17 break points he faced and striking 36 winners.

"I don't know," he said. "Right now at the moment it feels good. I've had some treatment, some medication, so hopefully it stays that way and gets even better tomorrow and (for the) upcoming match. We'll see."

Khachanov will have experience on his side. The Russian, who reached the US Open semi-finals in 2022, booked his seventh major quarter-final with a five-set win over 20-year-old American Learner Tien.

articles.title: The US Open wants to be for everyone. Not everyone knows the etiquette
articles.summary: The crowds at the US Open have been the dominant off-the-court storyline of the tournament. It might be a sign of where the sports industry is headed.
articles.body: It makes sense that the most attractive audience to any money-making venture is whatever one is still relatively untapped. We’re living in an era where success is measured not in sustainability or even sheer size but nothing short of endless, indefinite growth. For a tennis tournament, that tantalizing market of maybe-future customers means people who do not currently know or care all that much about tennis. There’s no moral judgement to that characterization. Ignorance or even disinterest about tennis is a perfectly fine way to be as a person. Provided you’re not attending a high profile — and increasingly prohibitively pricey — tennis match in cushy, comped seats. The US Open would like to believe those people are either fans who just don’t know it yet or that such a disposition does not preclude enjoying themselves at a tennis match. It probably doesn’t. The weather this week in New York has been mostly glorious. The grounds of the US Open are buzzing with beautiful people. The food options are decadent. The Honey Deuce is dangerously delicious (based on a single, very professional sip taken by this serious journalist). And yet, the discourse around the tournament centers on the “close to 100” credentialed influencers creating tennis-adjacent content a little too close to the tennis itself. In viral videos, content creators are seen filming during active moments in the match. There have been concerns about the use of ring lights or camera flashes during play. The umpires have repeatedly reminded attendees to quiet down in between games. During the first week of the tournament, players were asked about the potential distraction or disturbance of such a presence at the Open. Coco Gauff said the light was a bigger issue than the sound, “because that does bother – and I am one of the more lenient players.” For Naomi Osaka, it was the opposite. “There was a moment where there was, like, people shouting and stuff, and you could hear it quite clearly. I think it bothered my opponent, too,” she said. “I don’t really see the lights, because obviously, like, when you are serving, you’re looking at the sun or you’re looking at the night lights. It was more the noise.” Regardless of the specifics, the upshot was, as Jessica Pegula put it: “People are down there trying to perform, and it’s their career and their job. It seems a bit disrespectful.” According to ESPN, the people in the viral videos are not among those credentialed by the USTA. The creator credential, issued for the first time last year, encompasses social media editors associated with traditional outlets, tennis-specific independent creators, and lifestyle influencers focused on food or fashion. That doesn’t prevent other paying guests from using the Open as a stage for filming content. The individuals, however, are less interesting than the ethos it reflects (get any large enough group together – with ample access to alcohol – and someone will misbehave.) Sports are in the midst of a global makeover from narrow manifestations of tribal interest to mainstays of the monoculture. Instead of meccas or meeting places for diehard fans, live sporting events try to position themselves as major cultural moments. It’s evident in the coverage – sports as soap operas, sports as fashion platforms or foodie destinations, sports as celebrity factories. It’s part of a larger everything-ization of, well, everything. Watch enough influencer content, for example, and they’re bound to say something about wanting their page to have something for everyone. That’s what success looks like these days: Being a brand with universal appeal. For sports this has been a boon and a bit of course correction. You can be a casual fan, a shameless bandwagoner. There’s less gatekeeping that, let’s be honest, disproportionately impacted certain demographics. There’s nothing wrong with being new to tennis. For their part, the athletes recognize that and the value of a broader audience. They are, after all, demanding increased prize money. “I have no problem with anybody doing anything, coming to watch the tennis. Putting asses in seats, you know, different age ranges, whatever, is huge for our sport,” Francis Tiafoe said. “That’s all I care about. “I can appreciate the influencers coming and kind of showcasing the US Open experience,” Pegula said. “I think that’s something that the US Open has utilized a lot as far as food and drinks and things to do and the shops. That part is part of a fan experience and something that people might not know and make them want to go.” “I definitely think it’s cool to have a new demographic and I definitely think it helps grow the sport,” Gauff said. “I think there is huge positives,” Osaka said. “Like, you want people to continue to grow the sport. I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette.” But of course, those are two sides of the same coin. Intrinsic to being new is having less experience. An audience of “everyone” includes those that do not know the rules and etiquette. That’s not to absolve individuals from common sense or basic decency. But, come on, you’ve been outside before, do you really think everyone has that? The truth is, it seems plenty of people who paid to be at the US Open don’t totally know the etiquette or are a little tipsy – or perhaps both. At a Labor Day evening match between Gauff and Iva Jovic, the US Open staff tasked with encouraging attendees to expediently find their seats were regularly so overwhelmed with the task that sterner-sounding staff in red SUPERVISOR shirts appeared to scold the patrons. Still, it proved to be a Sisyphean feat. It was a brilliant match, a stunning showcase of Gauff’s speed and power against a worthy up-and-coming teenage opponent. The crowd was, overwhelmingly, locked in on every volley, cheering in proportion to the intensity of the point regardless of which American player prevailed (spoiler: it was Gauff in straight sets). And yet, for the entirety of the hour-and-a-half match, guests had to be told to stop congregating in front of their sections where they were blocking other people’s sightlines – and where the views of the court were the best. Probably some, if not most, of them were taking pictures. You don’t have to be an influencer these days to prioritize evidence of your experience over someone else’s experiences these days. “They don’t listen,” an usher sighed seemingly to herself at one point. “Nobody listens.”

articles.title: Sabalenka se niega a entregarle el cetro de la WTA a Rybakina y pasa a semifinales del US Open
articles.standfirst: La kazaja será número 1 este miércoles si derrota a Zheng y se cuela entre las cuatro mejores
articles.summary: La kazaja será número 1 este miércoles si derrota a Zheng y se cuela entre las cuatro mejores
articles.body: Elena Rybakina tendrá que ganarse el número 1 en la pista. La kazaja depende de sí misma para convertirse en la trigésima tenista que lidera las listas del circuito femenino. Le vale con ganar este miércoles a la china Qinwen Zheng en los cuartos del US Open. Aryna Sabalenka, reina actual, no le facilitará las cosas para que la supere en la clasificación. Lo demostró este martes derrotando a Linda Noskova, flamante campeona de Wimbledon, por 7-6(1), 3-6 y 7-6(7), en el súper 'tie break'. La primera cabeza de serie del cuadro fue capaz de remontar un 4-2 adverso en la manga de desempate. A la conclusión, lanzó balones fuera acerca de sus ganas de seguir líder: "Estaré más que contenta si Rybakina se lleva el número 1 y yo gano el torneo". Ya son seis semifinales consecutivas en el Abierto de los Estados Unidos. Sabalenka se sitúa a 976 puntos de la kazaja. A la jugadora de Minsk la penaliza el no poder sumar en el torneo neoyorquino como defensora del título. Aunque lo que realmente le pasa factura es su pobre a partir del mes de abril donde no ha sumado un solo trofeo más a su palmarés. Cuartofinalista del Mutua Madrid Open y eliminada en la tercera ronda de Roma, no pasó de la antepenúltima ronda en Roland Garros. Y aún le fueron peor las cosas en Wimbledon, apeada en la cuarta ronda por Naomi Osaka. Antes de eso, una semifinal de Berlín con Jessica Pegula de verdugo. Sabalenka es ya la sexta jugadora con más tiempo de permanencia en lo más alto, con un total de 99 semanas. La cifra mágica del 100 ya no está en sus manos. Desde Serena Williams (2012-14) ninguna profesional ha sido capaz de ganar tres veces consecutivas en las pistas de Flushing Meadows. Está a dos triunfos de hacerlo. Es lo único que le vale para mantener el número 1. Y en la misma carambola se encuentran Pegula y Coco Gauff. Su sueño de ser la mejor pasa ineludiblemente por levantar el trofeo de campeona del Abierto de los Estados Unidos. Coco ya conoce esa sensación. Lo hizo en la edición de 2023.

articles.title: US Open 2026: Aryna Sabalenka outlasts Linda Nosková in grueling quarterfinals match
articles.summary: Linda Nosková was the first competitor to take a set off Aryna Sabalenka at the 2026 US Open.
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka entered the 2026 US Open with one goal: To become the third woman to win the event in three straight years. That goal nearly died Tuesday, as Sabalenka was pushed to the limit by Linda Nosková.

In the end, Sabalenka just barely prevailed, advancing to the semifinals after taking down Nosková in three sets (7-6, 3-6, 7-6). It took two tiebreak wins from the women's No. 1, who was in danger of being eliminated by Nosková a handful of times during the nearly two-and-a-half-hour match.

Sabalenka got off to an excellent start, taking the first seven points off Nosková to take an early lead. She finally allowed Nosková to pick up her first point in the second game, but Sabalenka took the game on the next point, going up 2-0.

It took until the fourth game of the first set for Nosková to pick up a win. Sabalenka kept it close, but dropped to 3-1 in the set. Nosková seemed to gain steam from there, eventually clawing her way all the way back to tie the first set at 5-5. After such a strong start, Sabalenka was suddenly looking at a surprising loss in the first set.

But Sabalenka rallied, eventually forcing a tiebreak. She then jumped out to an impressive lead in that tiebreak, winning the first six points before Nosková finally earned a point. Sabalenka didn't allow a comeback, winning the next point to take the first set 7-6. It was hard fought, but Sabalenka was a set away from making it to the semifinals.

Nosková seemingly fully recovered after her early-match struggles, and managed to go ahead 2-1 in the second set. Sabalenka battled back to even the set, and it looked as though both players would once again engage in a lengthy back-and-forth.

But that wasn't the case. Nosková fully found her stride, taking the next three games to make it 5-2. Sabalenka managed to take the next game, but couldn't hold off Nosková, who won the set 6-3.

It was the first set Sabalenka dropped at the 2026 US Open. It also marked the first time in their head-to-head careers that Nosková took a set off Sabalenka.

After registering eight aces in the first set — which she lost — Nosková seemed to play a better all-around game in the second set. She registered four aces and limited her unforced errors to take the set. Though she missed out on some aces, Nosková posted an 83% win rate with her first serve, so it was clearly still very effective even if Sabalenka was able to return it slightly more often.

Nosková kept that momentum going in the final set. With the pair tied 2-2, Nosková won the next two games to take a lead in the final set. Her serve looked strong yet again, picking up three aces to that point.

Sabalenka quickly managed to bounce back, evening the set at 4-4. She then took the next game, putting her a game away from a victory. But Nosková tied things up yet again. The two traded the next two games, setting up yet another tiebreak.

Like the rest of the match, the tiebreak resulted in back-and-forth play from both competitors. With the tiebreak at 3-3, Sabalenka took the next three points. That wasn't enough, as the pair battled back to nearly even things up again. With the pressure on, Sabalenka went up 9-7. She took the match point on her next serve, finally defeating Nosková 10-7 in the tiebreak and winning the match.

Despite their high WTA rankings, Sabalenka and Nosková had not faced each other much in singles play. Coming into Tuesday's match, Sabalenka held a 2-0 lead over Nosková in head-to-head matchups, the most recent of which came at the BNP Paribas Open in March. Sabalenka won that match in straight sets.

Things were much harder Tuesday, as Sabalenka's time in the tournament flashed before her eyes multiple times thanks to Nosková. Thanks to some relentless play and late-match execution, Sabalenka still has a chance to match Chris Evert and Serena Williams as the only women to win three straight US Opens.

After a hard-fought win over Nosková, Sabalenka will get a day of rest Wednesday before the semifinal Thursday. If she can win that match, she'll be just one more victory away from equaling two of tennis' most decorated stars.

articles.title: Inspiring story on finding strength: “When you’re down and it feels impossible, that’s the moment that defines you”- How Alexander Zverev turned career setbacks into Grand Slam glory
articles.summary: International Sports News: Alexander Zverev has spent much of his tennis career learning how to deal with difficult moments. From losing Grand Slam finals to suffering a serious.
articles.body: Alexander Zverev has spent much of his tennis career learning how to deal with difficult moments. From losing Grand Slam finals to suffering a serious ankle injury that kept him out for months, the German has had several moments when his career could have gone in a very different direction.That is why his words, “When you’re down and it feels impossible, that’s the moment that defines you,” carry a deeper meaning when looked at alongside his journey.Zverev is no stranger to being close to the top and then having to start again. He lost the 2020 US Open final after leading Dominic Thiem by two sets. In 2022, he suffered a serious ankle injury during his French Open semifinal against Rafael Nadal.He later returned to the tour, worked his way back to the top level and finally won his first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros in 2026. The quote is simple, but each part tells a story about dealing with failure, doubt and pressure.What does “when you’re down” really mean?Being “down” does not always mean losing a tennis match. For an athlete, it can mean losing confidence, dealing with an injury or simply feeling that things are no longer going the way they once did.Zverev has experienced all of those situations.His 2022 French Open injury was one of the lowest points of his career. He was playing Nadal in the semifinal and had been involved in a thrilling battle when he badly rolled his right ankle. Zverev had torn all three lateral ligaments in the ankle and needed surgery. He did not play another competitive match that year.The timing made the injury even harder to accept. Zverev was already one of the best players in the world and was pushing for his first Grand Slam title. The injury suddenly stopped everything.But being down did not mean his story was over.He returned in 2023 and initially struggled. He later explained that he was still dealing with pain and could not move around the court in the same way. Yet he slowly found his level again, winning titles in Hamburg and Chengdu and returning to the ATP Finals.Why does “it feels impossible” matter?This is perhaps the most important part of the quote. When something feels impossible, there is no guarantee that things will get better. That is what makes those moments so difficult.Zverev knew that feeling after his ankle injury. Even his family could not be certain that he would return to his previous level. Ahead of the 2026 US Open, Zverev spoke about those doubts and said his family never showed them to him. Instead, they talked to him about getting better and becoming one of the best players again.That support mattered because Zverev had already experienced another kind of pain: coming close to a Grand Slam title without winning one.He lost his first major final at the 2020 US Open after taking a two-set lead against Thiem. He then lost the 2024 French Open final to Carlos Alcaraz after leading by two sets to one. He also finished runner-up to Jannik Sinner at the 2025 Australian Open.After so many close calls, it would have been easy to believe that a Grand Slam title might never come. But Zverev kept trying.How can the hardest moments define a player?The quote suggests that a player is not truly defined by the easy wins. The real test comes when confidence disappears and there is a reason to give up.Zverev’s career is a strong example of that idea.After his ankle injury, he had to rebuild his game and his confidence. His return was not perfect. He had to accept that he could not immediately be the same player he had been before the injury.He also had to deal with the mental weight of his Grand Slam losses.That became clear during the 2026 French Open final. Zverev was physically struggling against Flavio Cobolli and admitted afterward that some of his problems were mental.He said he had become tense and emotional, but eventually he was able to let go and play more freely. He won the five-set match 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7(5), 6-1 to finally become a Grand Slam champion.That victory changed the meaning of many of his previous disappointments. The injury did not disappear. Neither did the losses. But they became part of the road that eventually took him to his first major title.What does Zverev’s journey teach us about the quote?The final part, “that’s the moment that defines you”: is really about what a person does after reaching their lowest point. Zverev could have allowed the ankle injury, the Grand Slam losses or the doubts surrounding his career to become the defining parts of his story.Instead, he kept coming back. His 2026 French Open victory was the biggest proof of that. After three previous Grand Slam final losses, Zverev finally lifted a major trophy at 29. The victory also made him the first German men’s champion in the Open Era at Roland Garros.And his story is still being written. At the 2026 US Open, Zverev reached the quarterfinals after beating Luciano Darderi in straight sets. The result made him the only man to reach the quarterfinals at all four Grand Slams in 2026.That is why the quote feels particularly fitting for Zverev. Being down is not the end. Feeling that something is impossible does not mean it cannot happen. The real test is what comes next. For Zverev, the answer has been simple: keep going.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: US Open 2026: Aryna Sabalenka edges into semi-finals with three-set win over Linda Noskova in thriller
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka retains world No 1 spot with battling win - but will lose it on Wednesday if Elena Rybakina reaches semi-finals; Sabalenka is looking to become first woman to win US Open three times in row since Serena Williams between 2012 and 2014; watch tournament live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The 28-year-old beat Noskova 7-6 (7-1) 3-6 7-6 (10-7), coming through two tie-breaks - and a 4-2 deficit in the final set - as she sealed victory with a second-serve ace to set up a meeting with the winner of Tuesday night's all-American clash between Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro in the semi-finals.

Sabalenka needs to win in New York to have any hope of staying as world No 1 but will definitely lose that spot if Elena Rybakina - who defeated Sabalenka in this year's Australian Open final - overcomes Qinwen Zheng in her quarter-final on Wednesday.

If Rybakina is beaten, then Pegula or Coco Gauff could rise to the top of the rankings should they win the tournament at Flushing Meadows on Saturday evening.

Sabalenka, world No 1 for 99 consecutive weeks, is hoping to become the first woman to win the US Open three times in a row since Serena Williams from 2012-14.

Noskova, who had forced a first-set tie-break from 5-2 down, double faulted at 3-3 in the final-set breaker and then slipped 8-6 down after an unfortunate net cord, before Sabalenka, who has never lost a US Open quarter-final and won her last 10 tie-breaks at the event, edged into the last four.

Sabalenka extended her career record over Noskova to 3-0 after previously seeing off the 21-year-old in the Adelaide International final in 2023 and then the Indian Wells semi-finals earlier this year.

Noskova will not become the first woman to secure back-to-back Grand Slams since Naomi Osaka claimed the 2020 US Open and 2021 Australian Open after seeing her 11-match winning streak in majors come to an end.

Aryna Sabalenka , speaking in her on-court interview:

"Thinking the match is over is probably what helped me to feel loose, go for my shots. I am super happy to get this win - a tough match, tough battle.

"These kind of crowds, tie-breaks, and these matches that are such high pressure boost my confidence and my energy.

"For now I just want to relax, recover, and reflect on what happened."

Sabalenka broke Noskova to love in the second game of the match en route to a 5-2 lead, only to them lose four of the next five games as her Czech opponent fought back to 6-6.

The first-set tie-break, however, was completely one-sided with Noskova's only point coming via an ace out wide as her double fault and Sabalenka's power settled things.

Noskova staved off break points early in the second set, including in the first game, and carved out two of her own on the Sabelanka serve at 3-2 up, taking the second of those when her rival produced an untimely double fault.

Sabalenka saved break point with an ace in her subsequent service game before Noskova went on to set up a deciding set by converting a fourth set point.

Noskova became favourite when she broke Sabalenka in the fifth game of the third set, with the world No 1 twice double-faulting in that game, but Sabalenka dug deep to level the match at 4-4 before the enthralled spectators were treated to another tie-break.

The second breaker was far more competitive than the first, yet Sabalenka came out on the right side of it once again to stay on course for a three-peat.

Henman: Sabalenka comes up with the big shots

Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman on Aryna Sabalenka:

"Some of her [bad form] has been in lesser tournaments, where her intensity and concentration hasn't been quite as good. But when you face someone the quality of your opponent, you have to stand and deliver.

"Her tie-break record is absolutely phenomenal.

"When it comes to the most pressure-packed moments, she's the one that comes up with the big shots."

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Aryna Sabalenka fights back against Linda Noskova to keep title defence alive
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka battles back to beat sixth seed Linda Noskova in three sets and advance to the semi-finals.
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka thought she had lost her US Open crown before leaving herself "speechless" as she battled back to beat Linda Noskova in three sets and advance to the semi-finals.

Taken to a deciding set for the first time in this year's tournament, the two-time defending champion trailed 4-2 in the third set and later 2-0 in the tie-break before recovering to close out a 7-6 (7-1) 3-6 7-6 (10-7) win in a little under two and a half hours.

It was the 28-year-old's 19th consecutive win at the tournament, having not tasted defeat since the 2023 final, while she becomes the first woman since Serena Williams in 2016 to reach six successive semi-finals at Flushing Meadows.

Victory also sees her temporarily keep hold of her world number one ranking, though she will be overtaken at the top regardless of how she fares in the remainder the tournament if world number two Elena Rybakina beats Zheng Qinwen on Wednesday.

Sabalenka will next face either American third seed Jessica Pegula or her compatriot Emma Navarro, seeded 26th, as she bids to reach a fourth consecutive US Open final.

The Belarusian has a history of letting her emotions get the better of her, most recently in her quarter-final defeat from a set up at the French Open .

But as in her previous match against Taylor Townsend , when she had her serve broken four times and trailed 3-1 in the second set, Sabalenka showed impressive composure to emerge victorious against Wimbledon champion Noskova, suggesting she may have turned a corner.

"I'm speechless right now. I was pushing to the limit in this match, especially in the third set," said Sabalenka.

"I honestly thought that that's it, the match is over, but probably that's what helped me to feel loose and go after my shots. [I'm] super happy to get the win."

Fighting to stay No 1 - Sabalenka's US Open mission

Listen: Sabalenka beats Noskova in epic, and do we need five sets?

Asked in her press conference about the ongoing battle for the number one ranking, Sabalenka insisted her priority is retaining her US Open title.

"I'll be more than happy. Three-peat - sounds great," she said.

Sabalenka began the match in cruise control, breaking in sixth seed Noskova's opening service game and racing into a 5-2 lead, before being broken as she served for the set.

Although she dominated the subsequent tie-break, the double fault she hit in her last service game – one of four in the match – would prove a feature of her performance, as would her failure to convert break points.

She wasted three early in the second set before conceding a break in the sixth game with a double fault at 30-40 as Noskova forced a decider.

After hitting two more double faults to be broken for a third time, she looked down and out after Noskova held to love for a 4-2 lead, but won the next three games to turn the match around.

She then won the tie-break - for a 10th successive time at the US Open, in a run dating back to 2021 - to complete her comeback, sealing the victory with a nerveless second-serve ace.

This was only Sabalenka's second quarter-final victory since March, with the top seed unable to replicate her early season hard-court success – which included titles in Brisbane, Indian Wells and Miami – on the clay or grass.

She suffered last-16 exits in Toronto and Cincinnati in the build-up to the US Open, but has rediscovered something approaching her best form at the tournament where she is yet to lose a quarter-final in six attempts.

"I have to say that knowing that physically my body can handle these matches again, I'm super happy with that," Sabalenka said.

"And of course, these kind of tight matches give you so much confidence that you're back and you're ready to do anything it takes to get the win. So this match definitely gives me a boost of energy and motivation."

For Noskova, this defeat, during which she hit more winners, fewer unforced errors, and saved seven of her nine break points, ends a run of 11 consecutive singles wins at Grand Slams.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka beats Linda Noskova to reach US Open semifinals
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka edges Linda Noskova to keep alive hopes of a third straight US Open title.
articles.body:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka rallied in the final set to beat Linda Noskova in a match tiebreaker on Tuesday and reach a sixth straight US Open semifinal.

Sabalenka triumphed 7-6 (7/1), 3-6, 7-6 (10/7) over the 21-year-old Wimbledon champion, striking 42 winners but converting just two of her nine break point chances against the resilient Czech in a fierce duel on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Trailing 4-2 in the third, Sabalenka appeared headed for another Grand Slam disappointment in a season in which she has so far been unable to add to her stash of four major titles.

Clearly frustrated, Sabalenka nevertheless regrouped and broke Noskova to love to pull level at 4-4. They hurtled to the tiebreaker — where Sabalenka dropped the first two points before climbing back and finally sealed victory with a courageous second-serve ace.

Noskova fired 18 aces — 46 winners in all — as she became the first player to take a set off Sabalenka in the tournament.

“What a battle,” Sabalenka said. “I was pushing myself to the limit in this match especially in the third set.

“I honestly thought the match was over and that’s what helped me to feel loose and go for my shots.”

Sabalenka has now won 18 straight matches at Flushing Meadows, and she must keep going to a third straight title if she is to have a chance to retain the world number one ranking she has held since October of 2024.

The victory was Sabalenka’s first win over a top-10 player since she beat Coco Gauff in the Miami final in March.

That was her third title of 2026, but Sabalenka has struggled since, exiting early at both Roland Garros and Wimbledon.

The Belarusian will next face the winner of the all-American quarterfinal between third seed Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro.

Pegula is among the trio of players who arrived at Flushing Meadows with a chance to seize Sabalenka’s number one ranking.

A two-time winner on the WTA tour this year, 2024 finalist Pegula would have to win he first Grand Slam title to have a shot at the top spot.

She reached the US Open final in 2024 and owns a 4-0 career record over 26th-seeded Navarro.

Men’s defending champion Carlos Alcaraz faces his toughest test of the tournament, taking on eighth-seeded American Ben Shelton for a place in the semifinals.

Shelton expects to face a full-strength Alcaraz despite the fact that the seven-time Grand Slam champion is playing his first tournament in more than four months after recovering from a right wrist injury.

Alcaraz, who completed a career Grand Slam with his Australian Open triumph in January, has improved with every match and will likely need to do so again against Shelton, who is the leading contender to end American men’s 23-year Grand Slam title drought.

Two more Americans face off in Tuesday’s other men’s quarterfinal, with charismatic 11th seed Frances Tiafoe taking on 22-year-old Alex Michelsen.
